nodes.text:
Her sword comes up as you approach, and the point stays steady despite the blood on her habit.

"Far enough." Her voice is hoarse. "Another grave-robber come for the Barrowlight? You're the third this month. The other two went down those stairs and didn't come back up."
Sister Wren watches you over the edge of her blade, waiting.

choices.text: You're wounded, and you're afraid of something down there.
I'm not here to rob the dead. I'm here to end whatever is keeping them awake.
Step aside, Sister, or I'll move you myself.
I'll leave you to your watch.

nodes.text: "Sister Wren, of the Ashen Order. What's left of it." She laughs without any humor in it. "We kept the barrows of Greywater for three hundred years. Now there's me, a lantern that's gone dark, and a knight who won't lie down."

"Ser Halric." She says the name like a prayer gone sour. "The last champion of the Order. He swore to guard the Barrowlight until he was relieved of his watch. Then the Order dwindled, no one came to relieve him, and he went on guarding it after he died. Now the light has gone out, and he's still down there keeping his oath to a dead order."

She glances at the stair. "The door below is sealed with the Order's rite. If you don't know the rite, it bites."

You watch the way she favors her side, and the way her eyes keep sliding back to the stair. She isn't guarding the barrow from you. She's guarding you from it, and she is terrified she'll fail at that too.
Her face gives away nothing but rain and exhaustion.

For a long moment she studies you. Then the point of her sword drops.

"Gods help me, I believe you." She lowers herself onto a stone, wincing. "Listen. The door below opens to the litany: sun, then moon, then skull. And if you face Halric, don't just fight him. Speak the Rite of Rest. Tell him he is relieved. He was a good man once. He might still hear it."

She teaches you the words, and makes you repeat them until you have them right. Then she presses a small wax-sealed flask into your palm.

"Holy water, from the last blessing the Order ever gave. If the words fail, throw this. The dead cannot abide it, and Halric least of all."
"Pretty words." Her blade doesn't waver. "The last two had pretty words too. Go down if you must. I won't help you die."

Something in your face decides it for her. She backs away with her sword still raised until she reaches the edge of the gate's shadow.

"Then the dead can have you," she spits, and she is gone into the rain.
She laughs, low and tired. "I have stood watch over a dead knight for a month, stranger. You don't frighten me." She doesn't lower the sword, and she doesn't say another word to you.
"Still breathing, {player.name}. Good." Wren feeds another stick to her little fire. "Remember: sun, moon, skull. And speak the rite."

choices.text: I'll be back with the light.

nodes.text: She recites it once more, slowly, so you can't mistake it: "Halric of the Ashen Order, your watch is ended. You are relieved. Rest."

Wren rises when she sees the light in your hand. For a long moment she only stares at the Barrowlight, and something in her face that has been clenched tight for a month finally lets go. "You lit it," she whispers. "Gods above, you actually lit it."

Then the stone beneath your feet hums. A low bell-tone rolls up out of the barrow, so deep you feel it in your teeth more than hear it, and Wren goes very still.

"The stair beneath the sarcophagus," she says slowly. "The Order's oldest books spoke of it, and we all took it for a parable." She looks at the barrow as if she has never seen it before. "The barrow was never the tomb. It was the seal. Beneath it lies the Under-Barrow, the sunken halls where the first sleepers were laid, long before there was any Order to keep them. And that bell means they know the light is coming."

She tears a strip from her habit, binds her wounded side tight, and takes up her sword. "Go ahead with the light, {player.name}. Chalk the Order's flame at every turning, and I will follow your trail down into the dark. The Ashen Order does not end at a lichgate in the rain. Not while I can still walk."

choices.text: Then I'll meet you below, Sister.

nodes.text: Wren tests the knot on her bandage and nods toward the barrow. "Keep the light high and leave me a trail, {player.name}. I'll be right behind you."
Wren turns her back on you and stares at the barrow stair. She has nothing more to say to you.
